articles.headline: Longtime Lakers public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter dies
articles.description: Lawrence Tanter had manned the microphone in L.A. since the "Showtime" days until his retirement in June following a stroke.
articles.body:
Longtime Los Angeles Lakers public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter has died, the team announced Wednesday.

"We are deeply saddened to share the news of the passing of legendary Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter," the team wrote in a statement shared on its social media accounts. "For 43 years, LT's voice served as the soundtrack to Lakers games at the arena. He will be remembered as a cherished member of the Lakers family."

In June, the 76-year-old Tanter retired from his courtside post where he had manned the microphone in L.A. since the "Showtime" days of the 1980s.

Tanter had suffered a stroke late in the regular season and missed the Lakers' last six home games, plus the playoffs.

Last month, shortly before entering into hospice care, Tanter texted ESPN.

"Quote me," he wrote, "'It's been a blessing.'"

Known by Lakers fans simply by his initials, LT, Tanter was the longest-tenured PA announcer in team history and was recognized for his style as much as for his longevity.

Despite being equipped with a booming baritone voice and an imposing 6-foot-7 frame, Tanter's presentation relied on restraint, using a silky-smooth delivery to share the Lakers' starting lineups, substitutions, fouls and score announcements with an aim to inform rather than distract the audience.

Tanter channeled his parallel career as a disc jockey at various jazz radio stations in L.A. when he reported to the arena, often wearing an eight-panel cap atop his head and sporting a well-manicured white goatee on his chin.

Always part of the tapestry but never stealing the spotlight, Tanter's signature call became announcing "The Laker girlllssss" when the dance team finished a routine and scampered off the court.

Tanter's role was particularly poignant during the Lakers' most recent championship season in 2019-20. When the Lakers played their first game after Kobe Bryant's death in January 2020, Tanter introduced all five Lakers starters with the same line: "6-6, 20th year out of Lower Merion High School, Kob-eeeeee Bryant!" Later that season, when the Lakers competed in the NBA bubble in Orlando, Florida, and eventually won the championship, Tanter recorded player introductions at a home studio in the Porter Ranch area of Los Angeles that were played before Lakers games at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex.

The Chicago native played forward for his high school basketball team and received a scholarship to attend the University of Dubuque in Iowa.

He went on to be a part of 10 Lakers championships and 16 Western Conference titles.

"Lawrence Tanter has been an integral part of the Lakers gameday experience for more than four decades, setting the tone for countless memorable moments with his professionalism, energy and signature booming voice," Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss said in June when Tanter was shifting to an advisory role. articles.headline: 2026 MLB ABS challenge system tracker: Team, player rankings
articles.description: The ABS challenge system leaderboard ranks batters, catchers, teams and umpires throughout the MLB season.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball implemented the ABS challenge system for the 2026 season, which allows players to challenge a ball or strike call made by the plate umpire. Each team receives two challenges to start the game, and only batters, pitchers and catchers can challenge a call. If a team wins a challenge, it can keep challenging. If a team challenges incorrectly twice, it loses its challenges for the rest of the game.

Here are the ABS challenge system rankings for batters, catchers, teams and umpires for the 2026 MLB season.

Data updated through Wednesday, September 23.

articles.headline: Machado powers the Padres past the Dodgers 5-1, snapping Los Angeles' 11-game home winning streak
articles.description: — Manny Machado homered and drove in three runs as the San Diego Padres beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-1 on Wednesday night to take sole possession of the top spot in the National League wild-card standings.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Manny Machado homered and drove in three runs as the San Diego Padres beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-1 on Wednesday night to take sole possession of the top spot in the National League wild-card standings.


              The loss snapped the NL West champions' 11-game home winning streak and kept the Dodgers (97-61) from clinching at least the No. 2 seed in the National League and a first-round playoff bye. To secure that, they still need one win or an Atlanta loss.


              The Padres (88-70) were prevented from clinching their franchise-record third consecutive playoff berth when Arizona beat Colorado 5-3. But they need just one win or a Diamondbacks loss to punch their ticket to the postseason.


              San Diego leads Chicago (87-71) and Philadelphia (87-71) by one game for the first National League wild card, a spot that would bring home-field advantage throughout a best-of-three series.


              In his return from the injured list, Shohei Ohtani went 1 for 4 with a single, a walk and two strikeouts for Los Angeles. He went down swinging with the bases loaded to end the fourth inning. His long drive to center field was caught near the wall leading off the eighth.


              Dodgers starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9) retired nine of his first 10 batters before the Padres got to him in the fourth and fifth innings of his final regular-season start.


              San Diego grabbed a 2-0 lead on Machado's 409-foot homer to center that scored Dustin Harris, who was hit by a pitch from Yamamoto leading off the fourth.


              The Dodgers closed to 2-1 in the bottom half when Teoscar Hernández scored on Tommy Edman's sacrifice fly on the first pitch from reliever David Morgan. 


              The Padres extended their lead to 4-1 in the fifth on Yamamoto's second career throwing error and Machado's shallow sacrifice fly.


              Freddy Fermin's RBI single in the ninth scored Samad Taylor, who walked and stole second and third on consecutive pitches by reliever Blake Treinen, making it 5-1.


              Bradgley Rodriguez (4-3) got the win with two scoreless innings of relief.


              San Diego starter Robbie Ray allowed one run and seven hits in 3 1/3 innings with two strikeouts. The left-hander needed 70 pitches to get through the first three innings. 


              Up next 
              Padres RHP Nick Pivetta (3-2, 3.30 ERA) starts Thursday in the series finale against RHP Tyler Glasnow (5-1, 3.46).


              ------

articles.headline: Who has the most home runs for each MLB team all-time?
articles.description: Check out each team's all-time home run leaders.
articles.body:
No player in MLB history has hit more home runs for a single franchise than Hank Aaron, who launched 733 for the Braves. Every team has its own home run king and, as we progress through the 2026 season, a changing of the guard occurred in Kansas City.

On July 25, Salvador Perez climbed past George Brett on the Royals' all-time home run list after blasting his 318th career homer.

articles.headline: Walton homers and Bolte has 4 hits to lead the Athletics to a 7-3 victory over the Angels
articles.description: — Donovan Walton hit a three-run homer and rookie Henry Bolte had his first four-hit game to help the Athletics beat the Los Angeles Angels 7-3 on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Donovan Walton hit a three-run homer and rookie Henry Bolte had his first four-hit game to help the Athletics beat the Los Angeles Angels 7-3 on Wednesday night.


              Lawrence Butler had an RBI single and Walton hit his ninth home run, a two-out shot off rookie Walbert Ureña (9-11) for a 4-0 lead in the first inning.


              Bolte went 4 for 5, scored two runs and had an RBI double in the second that put the Athletics (63-95) up 5-0.


              Mike Trout and Vaughn Grissom hit back-to-back homers off Jeffrey Springs in the fourth to make it 5-2. It was the 22nd homer this season for Trout the 426th of his career. 


              Grissom followed his 13th homer with an RBI single in the fifth to cut it to 5-3 and chase Springs.


              Alika Williams and Bolte had singles off José Fermin in the sixth and both scored on a double by Shea Langeliers for the final margin.


              Springs gave up three runs on five hits in 4 1/3 innings. The left-hander was 3-0 after his first four starts, but went 1-14 over his final 25. Geoff Hartlieb (2-1) got five outs for the win and Elvis Alvarado struck out two in the ninth to close it out.


              Ureña yielded five runs on seven hits in four innings. The right-hander had allowed five runs in his previous three starts covering 21 innings.


              Athletics catcher Brian Serven fouled a bunt off his left eye in the sixth and had to leave the game.


              The Angels (60-98) are trying to avoid the first 100-loss season in franchise history.


              Up next
              Angels RHP Grayson Rodriguez (4-8, 5.96) starts Thursday in Seattle in the first of four games against the Mariners to close out the regular season. The Athletics haven't announced Thursday's starting pitcher for the first of four games against the visiting Astros.

articles.headline: Harrison Jr. blocking out noise amid slow start for Cardinals
articles.description: Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.

Harrison, who has one catch for 33 yards on four targets through two games, said Wednesday that he's not surprised by the reaction to his slow start, but said it hasn't been difficult to keep his confidence high. He didn't hesitate when asked where the level of it is, saying he has "a lot of confidence in myself."

"Does your confidence come from results or does your confidence come from your process?" Harrison said. "And I think for me it comes from my process. So, my process isn't going to change whether I get zero catches or 10 catches. I'm going to still do the same thing week in and week out, Monday through Saturday to prepare myself for games. So, I think that's where I have a lot of my confidence comes from.

"And obviously you want to have more of an impact in the game, but I think confidence really has to come from preparation more than anything."

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett said Wednesday that "nobody has lost confidence in Marv" despite his start, while Harrison didn't shy away from the reality, citing a number of reasons.

"It's definitely a combination of a lot of things," Harrison said. "For my route tree getting down the field, you need a lot of things to go right. You need the right coverage, you need protection to hold up, you need me to run a great route, you need obviously Jacoby to make the right pass and make the right read. So, I feel like it's never one person's fault for anybody's success or lack thereof, really.

"So, I think it's always a combination of a bunch of things and whether that's a lack of success or success in general."

Another reason, Harrison said, is because of the two defenses he's played this season. The Los Angeles Chargers gave him single coverage on just seven of 32 routes and the Seattle Seahawks are, simply, one of the best defenses in the NFL.

"Pretty much that simple," Harrison said. "Seattle's a really good defense and you don't want to give a lot of teams, especially a rival team, a lot of credit. But when you just look across the league, they're far beyond above everybody else, especially on the defensive side of the football. So, things like that happen."

Brissett said the two have had "good conversations" and has tried to lend an ear to Harrison whenever he needs it.

"It's easy to say, 'Oh, it's a long season' to other people, but to Marv it doesn't feel like it's a long season," Brissett said. "As a teammate and as a quarterback, you still have to be there for him because what if this week goes the same way? Am I just going to not be there? Manchester United have identified a new potential replacement for left back Luke Shaw. Plus, Erling Haaland is contracted to Manchester City for another eight years, but could Bayern Munich sign him? Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United and Liverpool are interested in Crystal Palace defender Tyrick Mitchell, TEAMtalk reports. The Red Devils reportedly see the 27-year-old as an alternative to Newcastle United's Lewis Hall as they continue plans to identify a long-term successor to Luke Shaw. Mitchell entered the final 12 months of his contract in the summer, and it is said that Chelsea are also monitoring his situation, attracted to the opportunity of landing him on a free transfer.

- Bayern Munich have emerged as suitors for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, according to TEAMtalk. The Bundesliga side are believed to see the 26-year-old as a potential future replacement for Harry Kane, who they want to remain at the Allianz Arena for a further two years before assessing whether a move for Haaland is possible. Meanwhile, TEAMtalk reports that Vincent Kompany's side are also keen on Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White, and could be contenders for his signature next summer amid plans to add him to their squad with England compatriot Kane.

- Chelsea and Manchester City are exploring a move for AC Milan forward Francesco Camarda, according to TEAMtalk. The Blues are said to have tracked the 19-year-old for some time, and they are monitoring whether an opportunity to land him could arise due to a lack of minutes for the Rossoneri since returning from his loan spell at Lecce. Camarda scored one goal in 21 Serie A appearances last season.

- Napoli are struggling to make progress in talks with the representatives of midfielder Kevin De Bruyne over a new contract, transfer journalist Nicolo Schira reports. Discussions have reportedly stalled with the 35-year-old, who arrived at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on a two-year deal in the summer of 2025, and it is now said that they are "on the verge" of parting ways next summer. De Bruyne was previously linked with clubs in Major League Soccer and the Saudi Pro League before deciding to join Gli Azzurri.

articles.headline: Sources: Mavs' Dereck Lively II (foot) not cleared for camp
articles.description: Dereck Lively II's status for the start of the season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources said.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN on Wednesday.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the past 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress.

Dallas begins training camp Saturday.

Lively has played a total of only 43 games in the past two seasons. He underwent his second surgery in December, ending his 2025-26 season after appearing in only seven games.

Lively, 22, the No. 12 pick in the 2023 draft, is entering the final season of his rookie contract.

If healthy, the 7-foot-1, 230-pound Lively could be a significant part of Dallas' long-term core as the Mavericks attempt to build a contender around reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

Lively, an athletic big man who is an excellent finisher and versatile defender, has career averages of 8.4 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 22.9 minutes.
